- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to model output.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5), model underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to compensate.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes in sentiment; apply a 1–3 day lag correction to avoid immediate overshoot.
- If model forecast exceeds true outcome by >3% for 3+ consecutive days, apply downward adjustment proportional to sentiment magnitude (e.g., sentiment = -0.4 → subtract 1.5–2.5%).
- Mean reversion bias: if model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture sentiment-driven momentum; weight sentiment history more heavily in final 5–7 days of forecast.
- If sentiment turns sharply positive after a negative streak, model tends to lag; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for next 2–3 days.
